newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW-Arcon Galmoy mine starts producing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Arcon Galmoy mine starts producing.

text.p: Irish exploration group Arcon International Resources Plc on Monday began production of Ireland's first commercial zinc mine in more than 20 years.

The Irish-owned Galmoy mine, located in the midlands county of Kilkenny, sent its first shipment of zinc concentrate to the southern port of New Ross on Monday, marking the culmination of an 85 million Irish pound project.
"Twenty years have elapsed since any company has developed a commercial zinc mine in Ireland," chief executive Tony O'Reilly jnr told Reuters in an interview.

"We are well positioned...we have a strong balance sheet, zinc prices are considerably higher than they were even two months ago and they are expected to increase quite substantially in the next two years," he said.
On current reserve estimates, O'Reilly said the Galmoy mine has a life of about 13 years.

"It has a nominal throughput per year of about 650,000 tonnes of ore. It will...produce in excess of 135,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate, which is what we sell to our six European smelters with which we have long term contracts," he said, adding Arcon had pre-sold 120,000 tonnes.
O'Reilly said zinc prices have rebounded considerably: "up about $200 per tonne in January and the market is expecting very much a bull run in zinc for the next two years as a minimum."

"We will be one of the lowest cost producers in the world and that obviously bodes well for us starting up at a time of resurging zinc prices; the dollar is also strengthening and that is also positive as our commodity is priced in dollars," he said.

O'Reilly jnr, son of Heinz chief and Independent Newspapers boss, Tony O'Reilly, said that from an operating point of view, based on current zinc prices, Arcon was well in the black in terms of operating profits.
"Our operating costs would be under $950 per tonne and zinc prices are $1,300 per tonne, so from an operating point of view ... at these prices we are well in the black."
He said he hoped the development of Galmoy heralded the renaissance of the industry and that there would be further mines and operations coming on stream in the future.
"In our licensing area we have substantially increased our resource base and we would be very optimistic that there are lots of targets and a lot of opportunities out there."

"You have the Lisheen mine, which is coming onstream in 2-1/2 years, so the more the world sees Ireland as a destination for zinc mining the more investment there will be and hopefully the more results will be achieved."
The Lisheen lead/zinc mine is a joint-venture between Ivernia West Plc with south African owned mining-based conglomerate Minorco SA. -- Dublin Newsroom +353 1 676 9779
